Suppose \(\mathcal C
e\varnothing\). Conditional on fixed finite arm counts \((n_z:z\in\mathcal Z)\), for every full-data rule \(\delta\), fixed nuisance point \(\eta^0\), and reduced law \(q\), the fiber \(\Omega(\sigma)=\{
u:S(
u)=\sigma\}\) is finite for every \(\sigma\), and \(\delta_0(\sigma)=\sum_{
u\in\Omega(\sigma)}K_{\eta^0}(
u\mid\sigma)\delta(
u)\in\mathcal A\). This rule satisfies \(R_q(\delta_0)\le R_{q,\eta^0}(\delta)\le\sup_\eta R_{q,\eta}(\delta)\). Conversely, every skeleton rule \(\phi\) lifts to the full-data rule \(\delta^{\phi}(
u)=\phi(S(
u))\), for which \(R_{q,\eta}(\delta^{\phi})=R_q(\phi)\) for all \(q,\eta\). Therefore \(\inf_\delta\sup_{q,\eta}R_{q,\eta}(\delta)=\inf_\phi\sup_qR_q(\phi)\). No pointwise inequality \(R_{q,\eta}(\delta_0)\le R_{q,\eta}(\delta)\) is asserted for arbitrary \(\eta\).
body.proof_tex:
Assume \(\mathcal C\ne\varnothing\), so each fixed \(\eta^0_z\) is a probability distribution on the off-target cells. For fixed finite arm totals and any skeleton table \(\sigma\), each coordinate of a member of \(\Omega(\sigma)\) is an integer between zero and the corresponding \(n_z\). Hence \(\Omega(\sigma)\) is finite.  By the multinomial theorem applied separately in every arm,
\[
\sum_{\nu\in\Omega(\sigma)}K_{\eta^0}(\nu\mid\sigma)=1,
\qquad K_{\eta^0}(\nu\mid\sigma)\ge0.
\]
Thus \(\delta_0(\sigma)\) is a finite convex combination of points \(\delta(\nu)\in\mathcal A\).  Convexity of \(\mathcal A\) implies \(\delta_0(\sigma)\in\mathcal A\); no closure or limiting argument is needed.

The experiment factorization shows that under \((q,\eta^0)\), the conditional distribution of \(N\) given \(S=\sigma\) is precisely \(K_{\eta^0}(\cdot\mid\sigma)\), independently of \(q\).  Convexity of \(a\mapsto\ell(a,Bq)\) and finite Jensen therefore give, for every \(\sigma\),
\[
\ell(\delta_0(\sigma),Bq)
\le
\sum_{\nu\in\Omega(\sigma)}K_{\eta^0}(\nu\mid\sigma)
\ell(\delta(\nu),Bq).
\]
The marginal distribution of \(S\) depends on \(q\) through \(Aq\) and does not depend on \(\eta\).  Multiplying by this marginal probability and summing over \(\sigma\) gives
\[
R_q(\delta_0)
\le R_{q,\eta^0}(\delta)
\le\sup_{\eta\in\mathcal E_{\mathcal C}^m}R_{q,\eta}(\delta).
\]
The first inequality uses only the conditional law at the fixed point \(\eta^0\); it does not compare the two risks pointwise at an arbitrary \(\eta\).

Conversely, for a skeleton rule \(\phi\), define \(\delta^\phi(\nu)=\phi(S(\nu))\).  Since both its action and its target \(Bq\) are functions of the skeleton parameter and skeleton data alone,
\[
\begin{aligned}
R_{q,\eta}(\delta^\phi)
 &=\sum_{\sigma}P_q(S=\sigma)\ell(\phi(\sigma),Bq)
   \sum_{\nu\in\Omega(\sigma)}K_\eta(\nu\mid\sigma)\\
 &=\sum_{\sigma}P_q(S=\sigma)\ell(\phi(\sigma),Bq)
 =R_q(\phi)
\end{aligned}
\]
for every \(q,\eta\).  Hence
\[
\inf_\phi\sup_qR_q(\phi)
\le\inf_\delta\sup_{q,\eta}R_{q,\eta}(\delta)
\]
by the first construction, while
\[
\inf_\delta\sup_{q,\eta}R_{q,\eta}(\delta)
\le\inf_\phi\sup_qR_q(\phi)
\]
by the lift.  The two minimax values are equal, with the inequalities valid as extended nonnegative real inequalities if a supremum is infinite.
body.justification: Because fixed arm counts and finite alphabets make every \(\Omega(\sigma)\) finite, the barycenter exists for every rule and lies in the convex action space without closedness or integrability conditions; likelihood factorization makes \(K_{\eta^0}\) independent of \(q\), and Jensen's inequality gives the first risk bound.
body.gap: Blackwell comparison does not directly apply because the conditional allocation kernel contains an unknown nuisance; the supremum over the variation-independent nuisance is the new step.
body.consumer: A minimax analyst loses nothing by storing and processing only target cells and total off-target counts.
